question.problem: The $10$th and $11$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $30$ and $33,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{10}=30$ and ${a}_{11}=33$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{11}-{a}_{10} \\  & =33-30 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{10}=30,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{10}$ is $9$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{10} & ={a}_{1}+9d \\ 30 & ={a}_{1}+9(3) \\ 30 & ={a}_{1}+27 \\ 30-27 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =3+(n-1)(3) \\  & =3+3n-3 \\  & =3n\end{aligned}
$$
